sentiment_reasoning: March CPI delivers a split verdict: headline surges to 3.3% YoY driven by a 10.6% energy spike from the Iran war, but core CPI comes in at 2.6% — below the 2.7% consensus — handing rate-cut bulls their first real data point in weeks. The 7-day ceasefire rally stalls in pre-market as futures flat-line ahead of the 8:30 AM print, then edge higher after the cool core surprise. Iran deadline extension hopes keep risk appetite alive, but oil's April 9 reversal higher and JPMorgan's zero-cuts call temper the enthusiasm. Net result: a slightly positive day that preserves the rally without extending it.

summary.gist: CPI day finally arrives after 7 days of ceasefire-driven rally — and the data delivers a split verdict. Headline inflation runs hot at 3.3% YoY (energy up 10.6% from Iran war), but core CPI cools to 2.6% YoY, below the 2.7% estimate. The cool core reading gives the Fed breathing room and lifts equities slightly. Iran deadline extension hopes add a second tailwind. The dominant trade today is buying the rate-cut reprieve in rate-sensitive names while watching oil for the next ceasefire headline.

executive_summary: US equity futures are flat to marginally positive in pre-market as investors brace for the March CPI report at 8:30 AM ET — the first inflation print since the Iran war erupted on February 28. The 7-day relief rally following the April 7 ceasefire announcement (Dow +1,325 pts, S&P +2.51%) has stalled, with the S&P sitting near 6,824. Oil reversed sharply higher on April 9 as ceasefire fragility resurfaced, pushing WTI back toward $90/bbl after briefly crashing 15% on the ceasefire news. The CPI print is the key risk event: headline is expected to show a 3.4% YoY print driven by a 10.6% monthly energy spike, while core is expected at 2.7%. The FOMC is on hold at 3.5-3.75% with one cut projected for 2026 — a cool core reading could re-energize rate-cut optimism and push S&P to fresh highs. Actual result: headline 3.3% (slight beat vs 3.4% est), core 2.6% (beat vs 2.7% est), 0.2% MoM (vs 0.3% est). Market closes slightly higher on the cool core and Iran deadline extension hopes.

macro_events.title: March CPI: Hot Headline, Cool Core — Split Verdict
macro_events.causal_chain: Iran war erupted Feb 28, closing Strait of Hormuz → WTI/Brent spike to $97+ → energy component in CPI surges 10.6% MoM in March → headline CPI hits 3.3% YoY (expected 3.4%) — slightly below consensus → BUT core CPI strips out energy, prints 2.6% YoY / 0.2% MoM (expected 2.7% / 0.3%) — cools below expectations → Fed's higher-for-longer narrative challenged at the margin → market re-prices one Sept cut as possible → growth stocks rally on lower discount rate → TLT/duration assets bounce → however, headline inflation 22nd consecutive month above 2% target → JPMorgan forecasts zero cuts → structural inflation risk remains elevated from tariff pass-through + energy
macro_events.geographic_dimension: US domestic consumer economy, imported goods inflation from China tariffs, energy cost pass-through from Middle East conflict
macro_events.historical_analog: June 2023 CPI: headline surprised lower (3.0% vs 3.1% est) while core remained sticky — produced a 1-day S&P rally of 0.9% but didn't sustain because the Fed's terminal rate thesis held. Current analog is similar: cool core gives hope but doesn't change Fed dots.
macro_events.counterargument: One month of cool core doesn't make a trend. Energy price declines from ceasefire could mechanically pull headline lower in April CPI (May release), accelerating disinflation narrative. But tariff pass-through (China goods re-priced as US-China truce extended) creates a floor on core goods inflation.

macro_events.geographic_dimension: Strait of Hormuz, Persian Gulf, global energy supply chains, Asian refining hubs, European LNG markets
macro_events.historical_analog: September 2019 Abqaiq/Khurais ceasefire resolution — oil spiked 15% day of attack then gave back 50% of gains within 10 days once supply restoration was confirmed. Current dynamic rhymes but Hormuz closure is broader scope.
macro_events.counterargument: Trump has domestic political incentive to maintain ceasefire — $5 gasoline is politically toxic. Back-channel negotiations with Gulf Arab states provide diplomatic support for extension. Iranian moderates also have economic incentive to maintain truce.

macro_events.title: Fed Higher-for-Longer at 3.5%-3.75% — April 29 FOMC in Focus
macro_events.causal_chain: March FOMC held at 3.5-3.75%, dot plot projects one cut in 2026 → FOMC minutes confirmed higher-for-longer, acknowledged tariff-driven inflation floor → today's cool core CPI (2.6% vs 2.7% est) provides first evidence the disinflation trend intact despite Iran energy shock → market re-prices 1 cut (previously near-zero probability by Sept) back to ~25-30% probability → 10Y yield dips slightly from 4.35% toward 4.25% → real rates compress modestly → April 29 FOMC: No action expected, but Powell press conference tone on 'data dependence' will be scrutinized → JPMorgan's zero-cut forecast vs consensus one-cut creates narrative tension
macro_events.geographic_dimension: US monetary policy with global spillovers: EM dollar debt, European rate differential, USD strength
macro_events.historical_analog: November 2023 FOMC pivot: Fed paused after 2.6% core PCE reading, sparking the Nov-Dec 2023 rally (+12% S&P in 6 weeks). Today's core CPI print rhymes but from different starting conditions (rates at 3.5% vs 5.25% then).
macro_events.counterargument: Energy-driven headline at 3.3% remains well above 2% target. 22nd consecutive month above target. JPMorgan projects zero cuts; if correct, current repricing is a head fake. Tariff inflation pass-through from China goods (even at extended truce 10% rate) puts floor under core goods.
